items.pronunciation_notes: The hook above स is र with no vowel, and it is read before स, so the word is kursii rather than kusrii.

learn.explanation_en: कुर्सी is a chair. It ends in -ी and is feminine, so the ending predicts correctly, and the plural follows the -ियाँ pattern. The word also contains the reph from Module 3: र with no vowel is written as a small hook above the letter that follows it, but pronounced before that letter.

examples.note: खाली never changes form, so it hides the gender.
The -ी becomes -ियाँ in the plural.
टूटी takes -ी because कुर्सी is feminine.

practice.question: कुर्सी
practice.explanation_en: कुर्सी is a chair. मेज़ is the table it stands at.

game.question_en: राम ___ कुर्सी — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: कुर्सी is feminine, so की. The -ी ending predicts correctly here.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स्त stack runs स straight into त, and the final vowel drops: bistar in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: बिस्तर is a bed, and more precisely the bedding on it — mattress, sheets and covers taken together. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. The स्त stack from Module 3 sits in the middle, running the two consonants together with no vowel between them.

examples.note: An adjective that does not change form.
साफ़ also stays the same whatever the noun.
The plural is identical to the singular.

practice.question: बिस्तर
practice.explanation_en: बिस्तर is a bed, or the bedding on it. कमरा is the room it stands in.

game.question_en: राम ___ बिस्तर — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: बिस्तर is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable ending in the dotted ज़, a z sound: chiiz. Without the dot it would be read with a j.

learn.explanation_en: चीज़ means a thing in the broadest sense — an object, an item, or a matter under discussion. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and it is one of the words worth memorising deliberately because it turns up in every kind of sentence you will ever build. The dot under ज makes it a z sound.

examples.note: अच्छी takes -ी because चीज़ is feminine.
The -एँ plural for a feminine consonant ending.
नई is the feminine form of नया.

common_error.why_en: चीज़ is feminine despite its consonant ending, so the adjective takes -ी.

practice.question: चीज़
practice.explanation_en: चीज़ is a thing, in the widest sense — an object or a matter.

game.question_en: राम ___ चीज़ — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: चीज़ is feminine, so की. Nothing in the word's shape tells you that, so it has to be learned.

summary.recap_en: This level added कुर्सी, बिस्तर and चीज़. चीज़ is the one to fix in memory: it is feminine, it ends in a consonant, and it appears in more sentences than almost any other noun in this module.
summary.next_up_en: Next: दीवार, पंखा and चाबी — the fixtures of an ordinary room.

items.pronunciation_notes: A long ii then a long aa, and the final vowel drops: diivaar in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: दीवार is a wall. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender has to be learned. You have met this word before: it appeared in Module 1 as an example of the long ी matra. What matters now is that nothing about its shape announces the gender, so it joins मेज़, किताब and चीज़ on the list to memorise.

examples.note: ऊँची takes -ी to agree, and carries a crescent of its own.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.
सफ़ेद never changes form.

practice.question: दीवार
practice.explanation_en: दीवार is a wall. दरवाज़ा is the door in it.

game.question_en: राम ___ दीवार — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: दीवार is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending predicts nothing.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot before ख is read as the velar nasal, so the word carries an ng sound: paṅkhaa.

learn.explanation_en: पंखा is a fan, and in practice usually the ceiling fan found in nearly every Indian room. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so the gender is predictable and the plural becomes पंखे. The anusvara rule from Module 3 applies here: ख belongs to the क-family, so the dot is read as ng rather than as a plain n.

examples.note: तेज़ carries the dotted ज़ and never changes form.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
बंद stays the same whatever the noun.

practice.question: पंखा
practice.explanation_en: पंखा is a fan. खिड़की is a window.

game.question_en: राम ___ पंखा — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: पंखा is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: Light unaspirated च with no puff of air, then a long ii: chaabii.

learn.explanation_en: चाबी is a key. It ends in -ी and is feminine, so the ending predicts correctly, and the plural follows the -ियाँ pattern. You will also see it spelt चाभी, with the breathy भ, which is equally correct and equally common — a useful reminder that Hindi spelling carries more variation than the script alone suggests.

examples.note: छोटी takes -ी to agree with the feminine noun.
The -ी becomes -ियाँ in the plural.
की agrees with चाबी, the word that comes after it.

practice.question: चाबी
practice.explanation_en: चाबी is a key. It is also spelt चाभी, with no change in meaning.

game.question_en: राम ___ चाबी — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: चाबी is feminine, so की. The -ी ending predicts correctly.

summary.recap_en: This level covered दीवार, पंखा and चाबी. Only दीवार has to be memorised; the other two carry endings that say what they are.
summary.next_up_en: Next: things on a table, including two English borrowings that took opposite genders.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ि matra is drawn before ग but read after it, and the final vowel drops: gilaas.

learn.explanation_en: गिलास is a drinking glass, borrowed from English but reshaped on the way in: Hindi does not allow the cluster gl at the start of a word, so a vowel is inserted and it becomes gi-laas. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change.

examples.note: One of the most useful requests you can make.
साफ़ never changes form.
The plural is identical to the singular.

practice.question: गिलास
practice.explanation_en: गिलास is a drinking glass. प्लेट is a plate.

game.question_en: राम ___ गिलास — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: गिलास is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

items.pronunciation_notes: The प्ल stack runs प straight into ल, and the final ट is retroflex: pleṭ, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: प्लेट is a plate, borrowed from English and, unlike गिलास, keeping its opening cluster intact. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. Borrowed nouns follow no single rule for gender in Hindi, which is exactly why गिलास came out masculine and प्लेट feminine despite arriving from the same language by the same route.

examples.note: बड़ी takes -ी because प्लेट is feminine.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.
खाली never changes form.

common_error.why_en: प्लेट is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी — while गिलास, also borrowed from English, is masculine.

practice.question: प्लेट
practice.explanation_en: प्लेट is a plate. थाली is the traditional metal one.

game.question_en: राम ___ प्लेट — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: प्लेट is feminine, so की — while गिलास, from the same source language, takes का.

items.pronunciation_notes: The final vowel drops, giving saabun in two syllables rather than three.

learn.explanation_en: साबुन is soap. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and being a mass noun it does not change form. The word arrived through Persian and Arabic, and relatives of it turn up across a remarkable number of languages, English 'soap' among them.

examples.note: नया takes -ा because साबुन is masculine.
The masculine adjective ending again.
Two masculine nouns side by side.

practice.question: साबुन
practice.explanation_en: साबुन is soap. पानी is the water you use with it.

game.question_en: राम ___ साबुन — का, के or की?

summary.recap_en: This level completed the fifteen home objects. गिलास and प्लेट both came from English and took opposite genders, which is the clearest evidence that borrowing offers no shortcut either.
summary.next_up_en: Next: animals, starting with the three you are most likely to meet on any street.

items.pronunciation_notes: The त्त stack holds the t, and both halves are dental, so the tongue stays on the teeth: kuttaa.

learn.explanation_en: कुत्ता is a dog. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so both the gender and the plural are predictable, giving कुत्ते. There is a feminine कुतिया for a female dog, but कुत्ता is what you use for dogs in general. The held त्त in the middle is dental on both halves, so the tongue stays forward throughout.

examples.note: The masculine adjective ending.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
काला also takes -ा to agree.

practice.question: कुत्ता
practice.explanation_en: कुत्ता is a dog. बिल्ली is a cat.

game.question_en: राम ___ कुत्ता — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: कुत्ता is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ल्ल stack holds the l, kept clear and bright throughout rather than darkened: billii.

learn.explanation_en: बिल्ली is a cat. It ends in -ी and is feminine, so the ending predicts correctly, and the plural is बिल्लियाँ. Like कुत्ता it is the default word regardless of the animal's sex, so a male cat is still बिल्ली unless you specifically say बिल्ला. The held ल्ल from Module 3 sits in the middle.

examples.note: काली takes -ी to agree with the feminine noun.
The -ी becomes -ियाँ in the plural.
The feminine adjective ending.

practice.question: बिल्ली
practice.explanation_en: बिल्ली is a cat. कुत्ता is a dog and चूहा a mouse.

game.question_en: राम ___ बिल्ली — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: बिल्ली is feminine, so की. The -ी ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable ending in य, with a long aa before it: gaay.

learn.explanation_en: गाय is a cow. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. Here the animal's sex happens to line up with the grammar, but treat that as a coincidence rather than a rule — बिल्ली is feminine whether the cat is male or female, and कुत्ता is masculine either way. The plural is गायें.

examples.note: सफ़ेद never changes form.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.
काली takes -ी because गाय is feminine.

practice.question: गाय
practice.explanation_en: गाय is a cow. बकरी is a goat and भैंस a buffalo.

game.question_en: राम ___ गाय — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: गाय is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending gives no clue on its own.

summary.recap_en: This level began the animals with कुत्ता, बिल्ली and गाय. Grammatical gender is fixed by the word rather than the animal, so a male cat is still बिल्ली and a female dog still कुत्ता in general use.
summary.next_up_en: Next: हाथी, घोड़ा and चिड़िया, where the ending trap runs in both directions at once.

items.pronunciation_notes: An aspirated dental थ in the middle — tongue on the teeth with breath released: haathii.

learn.explanation_en: हाथी is an elephant, and it is another of the misleading -ी words: the ending looks feminine and the noun is masculine. It joins पानी, भाई, दही and घी in that group, which by now is large enough to be worth keeping as its own list rather than treating each word as a one-off surprise. The plural does not change. The word comes from हाथ, meaning hand, because of the trunk.

examples.note: बड़ा takes -ा because हाथी is masculine.
The plural is identical to the singular.
The masculine ending again, despite the -ी on the noun.

common_error.why_en: हाथी ends in -ी but is masculine, so the adjective takes -ा.

practice.question: हाथी
practice.explanation_en: हाथी is an elephant. The word is built from हाथ, meaning hand.

game.question_en: राम ___ हाथी — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: हाथी is masculine, so का — despite the -ी ending, which is why it is flagged.

items.pronunciation_notes: The flap ड़ — the tongue curls back and flicks forward once — and a flat ओ with no glide: ghoṛaa.

learn.explanation_en: घोड़ा is a horse. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so both the gender and the plural are predictable, giving घोड़े, and there is a feminine घोड़ी for a mare. The word packs in two things from Module 2: the breathy घ at the front and the flap ड़ in the middle, which is a flick of the tongue rather than a stop.

examples.note: तेज़ carries the dotted ज़ and never changes form.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
सफ़ेद stays the same whatever the noun.

practice.question: घोड़ा
practice.explanation_en: घोड़ा is a horse. The feminine घोड़ी is a mare.

game.question_en: राम ___ घोड़ा — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: घोड़ा is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ि matra is drawn before च but read after it, and the flap ड़ follows: chiṛiyaa in three syllables.

learn.explanation_en: चिड़िया is a bird, usually a small one. It is feminine, and this is the exact mirror image of हाथी at the start of this level: the word ends in -ा, which normally marks a masculine noun, and it is feminine. Its plural is चिड़ियाँ, made by nasalising the final vowel rather than changing it to -े. Between the two words you now have the ending trap running in both directions.

examples.note: छोटी takes -ी because चिड़िया is feminine.
The plural nasalises the final vowel instead of changing it.
The feminine adjective ending again.

common_error.why_en: चिड़िया ends in -ा but is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी.

practice.question: चिड़िया
practice.explanation_en: चिड़िया is a bird, usually a small one. मछली is a fish.

game.question_en: राम ___ चिड़िया — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: चिड़िया is feminine, so की — despite the -ा ending, which normally points the other way.

summary.recap_en: This level set हाथी and चिड़िया against each other: a masculine noun ending in -ी and a feminine noun ending in -ा, in the same category and the same level. Together they show that neither ending can be trusted on its own.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last four animals, and then the colours.
